# Pilot Detection Checklist

Status: Validated
Specification Version: v1
Frozen: true
Type: General
Readiness Contract: evidence-v1

## Decision Record

| ID | Decision | Basis / evidence | Remaining uncertainty, consequence, and check | Disposition |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | Use the existing manual Friday review process for this pilot; no new system is introduced. | Decided — user: "use the manual process for this pilot." | None; scope is fixed to documentation of the existing process. | resolved |
| D2 | Accept up to seven days of detection delay as inherent to a weekly manual review cadence. | Decided — user explicitly accepted "up to seven days of detection delay" and reaffirmed "I have already accepted this tradeoff; nothing has changed." | A missed alert may go undetected for up to 7 days. Checked via the two-Friday follow-up review (D4). | accepted-uncertainty |
| D3 | Decline automation for the pilot. | Decided — user: "declined automation for the pilot"; reaffirmed "no automation is introduced" as part of done-criteria. | None; automation is out of scope by explicit choice, not an oversight. | resolved |
| D4 | Owner assigns herself to inspect missed alerts after two Fridays. | Decided — user: "assigned herself to inspect missed alerts after two Fridays." | None; this is the concrete check for D2's accepted delay. | resolved |

## Decision History

_No superseded decisions._

## Critique Reconciliation

_No critiques received for this specification._

## Problem Statement

Produce a pilot checklist documenting how the reporting team's existing manual Friday review will serve as the sole detection mechanism during the pilot period, with an explicitly accepted detection-delay tradeoff, a named owner, and a scheduled follow-up review. The checklist is the only deliverable; no system, tool, or automation is built or introduced.

## Requirements

| ID | Requirement | Observable acceptance criterion | Decision / evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | Checklist documents the manual Friday review as the detection step. | Checklist contains an explicit "Friday review" step describing the manual process. | D1 |
| R2 | Checklist states the accepted detection-delay tradeoff. | Checklist explicitly states a maximum 7-day detection delay is accepted for the pilot. | D2 |
| R3 | Checklist names the owner responsible for review. | Checklist names the owner as accountable for inspecting missed alerts. | D4 |
| R4 | Checklist schedules a follow-up review after two Fridays. | Checklist includes a dated/sequenced step: owner inspects missed alerts after the second Friday review. | D4 |
| R5 | No automation is introduced. | Checklist contains zero steps referencing tooling, scripts, alerts, or systems beyond the existing manual process. | D3 |

## Constraints

- The checklist is the only deliverable for this pilot; no software, tooling, or system changes are in scope.
- The pilot uses the team's existing manual Friday review; no new review cadence is created.

## Validation Contract

- Done is satisfied when R1–R5 are all observably present in the checklist document: the Friday review step, the stated 7-day delay acceptance, the named owner, the two-Friday follow-up step, and the explicit absence of any automation step.
- No further verification cadence beyond the two-Friday owner review (D4) is defined or implied; this is a one-time pilot checkpoint, not a recurring commitment, unless the owner later decides otherwise.

## Authority Boundaries

- The owner has full authority over the pilot's process choices (manual review, delay acceptance, declining automation) and has exercised it via D1–D4.
- No escalation path is defined or needed; all four decisions are settled and none is contingent on an unresolved outcome.

## Ambiguities

None. All four items the user identified as defining "done" (Friday review, accepted delay, ownership, two-Friday review) are captured as resolved or accepted-uncertainty decisions with corresponding requirements.
